# Exact polyhedral hinge chambers and a sign-reversal budget

This is a necessary-condition theorem for an ACTUAL polyhedral H minimum. It retains the inside-support hinge omitted by the existing conservative separator. It does not assume that arbitrary attained minima are polyhedral or that approximating polytopes remain stationary. Nor does it claim that these necessary conditions already pay OC.

The signed facet-path admissibility and max-active speed formula are proved in `candidate f454ad16a82f70ca`. The exact finite contact cover is the already constructed H cover. Unlike a Clarke convex hull, the result below retains a separate feasible-chamber condition for every actual sign pattern.

## 1. Finite-dimensional actual directions

Freeze all ambient facet normals and all selected cap normals. Vary the offsets of the finitely many nonvertical ambient facets by an arbitrary real vector h. Pure-base facets remain fixed. Include an optional signed logarithmic buffer-scale direction s when the objective has an attained interior-scale minimum. Write v_F(h) for the inward speed of a sampled fiber facet F. It is the maximum of the finitely many constant inward speeds of its active ambient constraints. Thus each v_F is a convex piecewise-linear function of h.

These are actual positive compatible families on the same base for all sufficiently small positive or negative parameters. Their total volume loss is

    D(h)=sum_F |F| v_F(h).

On a chamber selecting one maximizing ambient constraint for every sampled facet, D and every H contact response alpha_ia are linear in (h,s). The group contact budget is

    alpha_i(h,s)=min_a alpha_ia(h,s).

The coefficients are exactly those of the proved H response, including its own-volume and covariance terms. No free concave parameter or old volume martingale is inserted.

## 2. The exact first-order cap loss

Fix cap j with continuous normal u_j!=0 and threshold derivative r_j. Put c_j=r_j/|u_j|. Let S_j>0 be the sum of its proper section coareas. Let B_j(h) be the linear boundary-loss contribution over strictly captured non-supporting facet portions. It includes all ordinary captured boundary pieces but excludes the supporting facet itself whenever the cap is supporting on that fiber.

The EXACT cap loss is

    R_j(h,r_j)=B_j(h)+S_j r_j
       +sum_(inside F) |F| max(v_F(h),c_j)
       +sum_(outside F)|F| min(0,v_F(h)+c_j).         (1)

At an inside support, the body interior and the captured halfspace point in the same direction: the surviving boundary is the more inward of the body and cap planes, so the loss is max(v,c). At an outside support the body inward direction is opposite: newly captured thickness is [-v-c]_+, hence loss -[-v-c]_+=min(0,v+c). These are actual volume shells, not independently chosen selectors.

The proper term is S_j r_j because moving the threshold inward removes that coarea times r_j. All support and boundary terms use ordinary fiber facet area. In d=1 facet area is H_0 counting measure. Since only offsets and thresholds move, all hinge arguments are CONSTANT over each supporting facet. This is why a finite polyhedral chamber decomposition is available; arbitrary facet rotations would need an additional analysis of sign regions within a facet and are not included here.

Every R_j is continuous piecewise linear in (h,r_j), and strictly increasing in r_j, with all slopes at least S_j>0 and at most its total possible section coarea. In particular its inverse in r_j is globally defined, continuous and piecewise linear.

## 3. Exact quantile equalization and descent

For group i let rho_ij>0 sum to one. There is a unique common loss L_i and threshold vector r_ij satisfying

    R_ij(h,r_ij)=L_i for all j,
    sum_j rho_ij r_ij=alpha_i(h,s).                  (2)

Indeed, write r_ij=R_ij(h,·)^(-1)(L). The weighted sum is a strictly increasing continuous function of L tending to both infinities. The actual quantile continuation in the H cover has

    q_i(t)=Q-t L_i+o(t).

It follows that the normalized body objective strictly improves if every group has

    L_i-beta D(h)>0

at a fixed-scale minimum, or

    L_i-beta D(h)+M tau s>0                          (3)

at the interior-scale minimum of beta_epsilon-tau log epsilon. All off-deepest gaps and contact convergence are exactly those already proved for the actual cover. Thus actual attained minimality excludes (3) simultaneously for all groups.

## 4. A finite collection of exact linear feasibility tests

Choose a branch for each of the following:

1. one maximizing ambient offset speed at each sampled facet;
2. one minimizing contact alpha_ia in each group;
3. body or section branch in each inside max(v,c);
4. zero or v+c branch in each outside min(0,v+c).

The branch inequalities are respectively

    chosen v>=every tied candidate v,
    chosen alpha<=every other alpha,
    v>=c or c>=v,
    v+c>=0 or v+c<=0.

On a chosen branch all expressions in (1)--(3) are linear. Include the linear equalities (2). The resulting system defines a closed polyhedral cone in (h,s,r,L). Every actual direction and its unique equalized thresholds belong to at least one of these finitely many cones; conversely, every point of a cone satisfying its branch inequalities represents the exact cap/contact/body response at that direction. Ties belong to multiple cones but have identical numerical response.

Since the system is positively homogeneous, a strict descent direction exists in that chamber if and only if the linear inequalities

    L_i-beta D(h)+M tau s>=1 for every group i        (4)

are feasible, with the scale term omitted at fixed scale. Therefore an actual polyhedral H minimum makes (4) infeasible in EVERY chamber.

Finite-dimensional Farkas duality can certify each infeasible chamber separately. The resulting dual coefficients need not agree between chambers. Replacing them by one arbitrary convex hull of branch gradients would lose the disjunctive condition just established. Conversely, this theorem is first-order necessity only: infeasibility of all these systems is not asserted to prove an actual minimum.

## 5. Exact reversal defect for an odd velocity subspace

For the remaining statements restrict to a linear subspace of actual offset/scale directions satisfying

    v_F(-h)=-v_F(h) for every sampled facet F.        (5)

This holds when there are no positive-area sampled-facet ties, or for directions giving the same speed to all constraints tied on each such facet. It is an explicit restriction, not an unproved general-position assumption. On this subspace D and each contact alpha_ia are odd linear functionals.

For any cap and any threshold r, (1) gives the exact identity

    E_j(h,r):=R_j(h,r)+R_j(-h,-r)
      =sum_(inside F)|F| |v_F(h)-r/|u_j||
         -sum_(outside F)|F| |v_F(h)+r/|u_j||.        (6)

All proper terms cancel. The positive inside variation and negative outside variation remain separated, with their true opposite orientations. This is more precise than treating the omitted inside hinge as an arbitrary nonnegative error.

## 6. One-group equalized reversal budget

Suppose there is just ONE actual cover group. For a direction (h,s), let L and r_j be its actual equalization from (2), with

    alpha=min_a alpha_a(h,s),
    spread=max_a alpha_a(h,s)-min_a alpha_a(h,s)>=0.

The reversed contact budget is exactly -alpha-spread. Let r_j^-(ell)=R_j(-h,·)^(-1)(ell) and define

    Delta_j=r_j^-(-L)+r_j.                           (7)

This is the exact threshold correction needed to change the reversed cap loss from its value -L+E_j at threshold -r_j to the reference common loss -L.

Actual minimality in both directions gives

    L-beta D+M tau s<=0,
    L^-+beta D-M tau s<=0,

so L+L^-<=0. The reversed inverse-budget function is increasing. Evaluating it at -L>=L^- and using its target value -alpha-spread proves

    sum_j rho_j Delta_j >= -spread.                 (8)

For a single contact, spread=0. Formula (8) is an exact nonlinear necessary payment between inside and outside hinges, not an average selector inequality. On every fixed chamber each inverse is affine, so it becomes an explicit linear inequality there. If E_j>0 then Delta_j<0; if E_j<0 then Delta_j>0. More quantitatively Delta_j is the signed integral of inverse section slopes between the losses -L+E_j and -L, with slopes bounded away from zero by S_j.

For one contact, a particularly simple necessary consequence is that at least one selected cap must satisfy E_j(h,r_j)<=0 for every actual direction and its positive-side equalization. Otherwise every Delta_j<0 would contradict (8). Multiple contacts permit exactly the spread term displayed in (8); it must not be dropped.

## 7. What remains unproved

The chamber conditions and reversal budget are exact at a polyhedral attained minimum with the stated frozen normals and actual contact menu. A general H minimizer has not been shown to be polyhedral, and no stationary approximation is asserted. Multiple groups give the full chamberwise system; the one-group reversal inequality cannot be applied separately to each group without an additional argument. Finally, no direction has yet been constructed that violates these necessary conditions whenever beta is below Gamma_d/2^n. Those are separate remaining obligations.
